summary: Game-boy's M6 playtest feedback: the street's flashing ground (a z-fight) fixed and repainted as a comic ground, the GO sting silenced, the player feeling the hits he takes (a bigger victim camera stack, an ink hurt vignette, the HP panel jolt), and every enemy's detail upscaled toward its concept (crease and valley ink from the dense mesh, island merge, no border relax, colour borders per texel, thinner lines)
read_first: docs/reviews/M6/fix-feedback.md (Game-boy's words, verbatim, and the three phase-1 packages), fix-feedback-2.md and fix-feedback-3.md (the detail rounds)
docs/milestones/M6-calls/<KEY>.md for the packages your lens covers: FB-FEEL, FB-GROUND, FB-DETAIL, DETAIL-2, ROLL-OX, ROLL-KICKER, ROLL-THUG, ROLL-PUNK, OX-2

lenses.brief: The five enemies after the detail recipe, judged in first person against their picked concepts (assets/source/concepts/m6/kicker_c.jpg, thug_b.jpg, bruiser_a.jpg, boss_c.jpg; the Punk's M4 concept and his veteran swap). The question is Game-boy's: does each look closer to its concept and less 'blobby' than M6, and is anything now worse than M6? Sources in captures_dir: r_kicker, r_thug, r_bruiser, r_boss (each 'Look: <label> at 1 m'), lineup, heavies (2.5, 5 and 10 m beside a Punk), dj, dk, dt, dp1, dox (each turned 0, 90 and 150 degrees at 1.6 m), dp2 (the Punk beside the veteran), dp3 (the Punk at 1, 2.5 and 5 m), damage ('Look: tune damage at 1 m': marks and blood on swatches, which now follow the per-texel borders), fight ('Mixed six, fight': the roster moving at 2-10 m, for crawl or shimmer of the per-texel colour borders and the new ink in motion, which no builder checked). The M6 'before' stills: captures/m6-final/r_*, lineup, heavies, and each package's A/B sheet in captures/m6-feedback-3/ab/ and captures/m6-feedback-2/. Check: (1) colour borders that follow the texture without stair steps or blotches; a dark texture patch now shown sharply where M6 averaged it away; (2) interior ink where the concept draws a line, and no scribbles where it doesn't (cloth valleys at 1 m); (3) line weight consistent across the roster; (4) damage marks and blood still per swatch (skin bleeds; a cap, beanie, strap, steel or the champion's belt scuffs but never bleeds) along the new borders; (5) the veteran Punk still clearly different at 5 m; (6) nothing crawls in motion at 5-10 m. Use docs/milestones/M6-codemap/art-chain.md §9's rubric per character where it helps. Each finding names the character, the distance and the still, and the config key or file that fixes it (each character's assets/source/characters/<id>/pipeline.json; the chain's keys are listed in docs/milestones/M6-calls/FB-DETAIL.md and DETAIL-2.md).

The world and the feel in first person: the ground and the hurt feedback, judged from captures_dir. Ground (FB-GROUND): drift ('Look: ground drift', a still and slow-moving view of the street floor; tools/ground_flicker.py <avi> [log] measures frame-to-frame change), tour ('Look: arena tour', every arena of Mission 1), walk ('Perf: level walk', god mode through the street and roofs, the same act as Game-boy's flashing report; the M6 before is captures/m6-feedback/before/walk/), run_street ('Run: held back' over the street's arenas 0-2, real fights). Game-boy's words: the ground 'blinks/flashes constantly' and should look 'like a comic book texture of some kind instead of a glitchy computer-scape'. Check: it never flashes or swims in motion anywhere a player walks (the street, the roofs' decks and drop floors, the boss roof); it reads as a comic ground against assets/source/concepts/m6/mood_street_a.jpg (flat tones, bold ink), not busy or camouflage-like; the 8 m repeat (a manhole every tile) isn't obvious; the far floor doesn't scribble or moire; doorways, kerbs and drops still read. Hurt feel (FB-FEEL): hurt ('Look: player hurt', a Punk jab and cross from the front, a Bruiser smash from the left) and the real hits in run_street and fight ('Mixed six, fight'). Game-boy's words: 'I got knocked down to almost half-health without even realizing anything was happening to my character.' Check: every hit he takes is unmistakable at the moment it lands, including from the side and behind; it says where the hit came from; it is not nauseating in a crowd (several hits in a row, the 7-degree finisher roll); the vignette reads over the new ground; a hit from behind isn't hidden by the HP panel; blocked hits and the hits he lands still feel as in M6 (SPEC §6). The GO sting: confirm from the logs or the code path that GO is silent and the CLEAR sting after the boss stays. Each finding names the act, the time or still, and the tunable or file that fixes it.

Code, tests, the pipeline and the ledgers, over the round's diff: git diff 663cafc...82bab12 (663cafc is the M6 head Game-boy played). Check: the contracts as landed against ARCHITECTURE.md's '### Playtest feedback: <KEY>' headings (FB-FEEL, FB-GROUND, FB-DETAIL, DETAIL-2, ROLL-OX, ROLL-KICKER, ROLL-THUG, ROLL-PUNK, OX-2); no numbers in scripts (feel numbers are tunables in tuning_data.gd's groups); the layer rules (HurtOverlay, the camera's victim stack and the HP panel jolt only read state and never write game state; the simulation never reads a camera); the texel swatch path (pipe_detail.py texel_labels and the RGBA mask with the 128/255 marker; toon.gdshader's texelFetch decode, the fade, the damage class and gloss following the slot; ToonMaterials.texel_swatch_uv mirrors the shader; an art without the marker renders exactly as before); the crease and valley ink and the island merge behind config keys whose defaults are the old behaviour; every character's run.py --check and player_run.py --asset player --check reproducible, gen_trim.gd --check (now with ground_sheet.png), gen_palette.py --check; the guards in tests/test_m6_feedback_detail.gd (_rolled_out: a character opts out by having its own tests/test_m6_feedback_detail_<id>.gd) and whether each per-character test can fail; shared tests a builder loosened (test_art_contract.gd and test_toon_glint.gd for the Punk's blue channel, test_art_heavies.gd's region filter, STROKE_PIECES_MAX 600 to 800); every ratchet loosened is logged with a reason in the roster file and the calls file and is no looser than needed (strain min_min moves for the Kicker 0.0367 to 0.0183, Ox 0.028 to 0.016, the Thug's per-clip figures, the Bruiser's D-9); the scene edits (boss_roof.tscn Ground y, roofs.tscn PenthouseFrontFloorShutter draw_box) touch no collider (tests/test_m6_colliders.gd); ASSETS.md rows for every changed asset (ground_sheet.png, every RGBA mask) are right (the Thug's builder overwrote the Kicker's mask row once; the lead restored it on merge); no key printed or written anywhere; Tripo spend this round 0.

common_note: State: m6/full-art-audio at 82bab12, PR #6 open and unmerged. The round merged nine packages on top of 663cafc (the M6 Game-boy played): FB-FEEL, FB-GROUND, FB-DETAIL (phase 1), DETAIL-2, ROLL-OX (phase 2a), ROLL-KICKER, ROLL-THUG, ROLL-PUNK, OX-2 (phase 2b); calls in docs/milestones/M6-calls/<KEY>.md. Suite at the merge: see the lead's note in HANDOFF (phase 2a's merge was 1983/1983 in 389 s, 0 error lines). Every run.py --check, player_run.py --check, gen_palette --check and gen_trim --check is YES. No Tripo or Gemini spent this round. Recordings in captures_dir, one folder per act (bot.avi, bot.log, sheets/; look acts have per-mark stills): r_kicker, r_thug, r_bruiser, r_boss, lineup, heavies, dj, dk, dt, dp1, dp2, dp3, dox, damage, hurt, fight (crowd bot); drift, tour, walk, run_street (level bots on mission1.tscn). Cut finer stills yourself with ffmpeg from bot.avi when you need a moment. Known and already on the lead's list (confirm or sharpen them, with the config key that fixes each, rather than re-discover them): the Thug at 1 m has a hard black patch over the right half of his face and bandana (the per-texel borders show a dark texture patch sharply), and the hoodie's valley ink scribbles across his chest; the Punk's vest valley ink is a little scribbly on the back and hem at 1 m; Ox's face at 1 m is a flat tan shape and his right sleeve's lower orange edge saws (in the texture); the Bruiser's stitched quilting isn't in the mesh (folds only), 20k gave nothing over 15k. Perf is the lead's (a quiet-machine compare against 663cafc), not a finding unless you see a hitch in a recording. Spec departures already ruled by Game-boy: the victim camera stack (README, 'ruled by Game-boy at his playtest (2026-11-05)').
